scope: Audit of onto-dev before RE-01; available is always qualified by notes, not full workbook/native certification. Evidence paths are repository-relative.

groups.note: Stable external graph IDs and typed directional adjacency; not compact reasoning IDs.
Sourced immutable bitemporal claims with four-valued lookup; confidence is metadata, not probabilistic inference.
Standalone rules are binary positive entity-only, constant predicates, single heads; graph property/Cypher literals and aggregates do not imply rule support.
Standalone hot relations contain Python Fact/string objects. Sampler compact arrays are not a reasoning dictionary/working-relation implementation.
Standalone set facts separate logical identity from Evidence references; explicit separate-world point publication exists. No general persistent relation/dictionary generation store.
No individual equality canonicalization, inequality, keys or cardinality semantics; named class/property equivalence is not sameAs.
Adapters authenticate and bind context/world/source policy/mapping/ontology and pinned horizons. No reusable relational plan cache/dictionary generation compatibility layer yet.

Pinned indexed claim/graph extraction exists in Python; not native batched predicate/world Arrow extraction. PyRex #31 is an upstream request, not a current scan API. Arrow ingestion does not provide this read path.
Finite safe positive rules, exact repeated-variable unification, synchronous delta rounds with each body occurrence as a pivot. Per-atom variants run dynamically, not reusable native plans.
Python fact indexes/hash membership, nested-loop equijoins, head projection, set difference and per-run delta lifecycle exist. No generic vectorized relational operator API or persistent lifecycle.
No standalone sort-merge, semantic anti-join, vectorized/native/parallel fixpoint, differential weights or spill engine. Counter bounds do not guarantee exact RSS/GIL release.
Dynamic smallest-bound-bucket choice uses current index bucket sizes. Not a cost-based optimizer, skew/cardinality statistics catalog or operator selector.

Validated binary typed entity/variable rules, ontology-to-rule compilation and predicate-triggered dispatch exist. No reusable physical graph, SCC/negative strata, literals or affected-predicate incremental queue.
No goal specialization, magic sets, explicit negative rule premises or closed-world negation. Result.match filters an already computed closure.
Selected gestalt-core-v1 named-entity axioms compile to positive rules, with exact origin tables. No full RDFS/OWL claim.
Transitive closure is correct and bounded via Python indexed joins; the workbook's native-loop performance criterion is not delivered.

Only named selected axioms compile; no restrictions/chains/disjointness, datatype or shape reasoning. Explicit conflicting claims are non-explosive, not a selectable classical validation/profile implementation.
Full OWL DL remains explicitly out of scope; RE-24 requires an algorithmic/termination decision, with no JVM integration.

Legacy graph rules persist versioned multi-support justifications and reconcile via recomputation; standalone proofs are single-witness only. Point publication has commit visibility and caller-managed orphan recovery, not general incremental support/generation/checkpoint machinery.
No B/F deletion, minimal/top-k proofs, confidence calculus, automatic cross-world inference or temporal-modal closure. Existing bounded modal point queries are separate.
Storage temporal algebra and pinned horizons, legacy point premise intersection, bounded separate-frame modal evaluation exist. These do not constitute full-range standalone closure.
Standalone inference and managed publication are point-scoped. No complete interval-set closure, interval-native joins or temporal delta maintenance.
Existing optional PyRex native Arrow ingestion is unrelated to relational batch reads or recursive reasoning execution.

Deterministic inference/proof counters, isolated benchmark timeouts, staged timings and RSS exist. No native operator telemetry, production cooperative cancellation, runtime explain plan, incremental benchmark coverage or spill metrics.
Independent finite grounding, randomized parity, selected-fragment optional OWL-RL and deterministic witness tests exist for Python v1 only. No native relational engine property certification.
Strict bounded offline RDF normalization supports only selected named axioms. Incomplete imports require explicit acknowledgement; not general RDF/OWL profile support.
